title: docs(fields): the number page and catalog teach `scale` for the decimal width (objectui#11413)
body:
Fixes #11413

Clause-②: no

## What this changes

Every number face reads its decimal width from `scale`: `NumberField` derives its input `step` from it, and `NumberCellRenderer` reads it through `resolveFieldScale` (`@objectstack/spec/data`). Neither reads `precision`, which the spec declares as the total digit count. The number docs page and its catalog entry still taught `precision` as the decimal width, so a copied example stepped by `any` and showed the value's natural precision instead of the two decimals the page promised. This is the number twin of objectui#11255 (percent, PR objectui#11411) and takes the same shape.

- `content/docs/fields/number.mdx`
  - the heading `## With Precision` is now `## With Decimal Places`, embedding `fields-number/with-decimal-places`;
  - the intro line now reads "with an optional number of decimal places (`scale`)" instead of "with optional precision control";
  - the Cell Renderer comment names `scale` and the two widths a stored `1234.5` shows: `1,234.50` with `scale: 2`, and `1,234.5` with no `scale`. It replaces the unbacked `Example: 1,234.56`;
  - the Field Schema snippet (`precision: 10, scale: 0`) was already right and is unchanged.
- `examples/schema-catalog`
  - `fields-number/decimal-numbers` is renamed `fields-number/with-decimal-places` (title "With Decimal Places", slug-derived) and declares `scale: 2`. `precision` is dropped, not kept: the entry never used it to mean total digits, and the percent twin took the same route;
  - `src/index.ts` is regenerated by `scripts/regenerate-catalog-index.py` (not hand-edited), and `--check` reports it up to date. The renamed entry now sorts after `range-validation`.
- New pin `examples/schema-catalog/test/fields-number-scale-11413.test.tsx`
  - renders the corrected entry through the real `SchemaRenderer`, form renderer and `@object-ui/fields` registration, and asserts the input `step` is `0.01`;
  - renders the entry's own field through `NumberCellRenderer` and asserts a stored `1234.5` shows `1,234.50`;
  - each reading has a control: the same entry with `scale` moved back to `precision`, which is exactly the old entry, must step by `any` and show `1,234.5`.

No other file names the old id: `git grep decimal-numbers` at the base gave the docs page and `index.ts` only. No snapshot or census pins it. The pin reads no markdown, so `scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs` needs no row (`--audit` is green).

## Premise check (at base `e0a9c6760`)

- The page headed the example `## With Precision` and embedded `fields-number/decimal-numbers`. The intro said "with optional precision control", and the Cell Renderer comment said "Renders with precision and tabular-nums font". `decimal-numbers.json` declared `"precision": 2` and no `scale`.
- Measured through the real renderers, not read off the code (the pin's control legs are the old entry exactly):

| reading | before (`precision: 2`) | after (`scale: 2`) |
|---|---|---|
| input `step` | `any` | `0.01` |
| `NumberCellRenderer`, stored `1234.5` | `1,234.5` | `1,234.50` |

## Ablations (one-shot, from the committed state `f79993d62`)

Each ran through `ablation-replace.mjs` with an on-disk mutation proof and a proven restore (blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty).

- A. `NumberField` step pointed at `precision` instead of `scale`: predicted 1 red / 1 green, observed `Tests 1 failed | 1 passed (2)` (`expected 'any' to be '0.01'`).
- B. Catalog entry `"scale": 2` back to `"precision": 2`: predicted 2 red, observed `Tests 2 failed (2)`. The step test stops at its key assertion (`expected undefined to be 2`), and the cell test reads `1,234.5`.
- C. `NumberCellRenderer` pointed at `precision`: predicted 1 red / 1 green, observed `Tests 1 failed | 1 passed (2)` (`expected '1,234.5' to be '1,234.50'`).

`@object-ui/fields` resolves to `packages/fields/src` through the root vitest alias, so A and C needed no rebuild to reach the test.

## Acceptance notes

- Out of scope, measured, not touched: the read-only face of `NumberField` ignores `scale`. A form field declared `type: 'number', readonly: true` with a stored `1234.5` shows `1234.5` both with `scale: 2` and with no `scale` (a temporary probe through the real form renderer, deleted), while the table cell shows `1,234.50`. It is in the dev report for the seat. This page makes no claim about the read-only display, so nothing here depends on it.
- Install note: this container's node is 22.22.0, below `jsdom@30`'s engines floor, and the repo sets `engine-strict=true`. The worktree was therefore installed with `pnpm install --config.engine-strict=false`, which changed no tracked file. CI is unaffected.
